intent.quote: I wont review the concept spec or any plan. use agents that verify that my intent based on that conversation is respected. I want to have the implementation available by tomorrow morning (in 9 hours).
intent.readback: Your words are approximate, so the agent turns them into formal intent and requirements, and a judge checks that interpretation against what you said and the context you said it in. A checked interpretation counts as your approval, marked as the judge's, with the trail back to your sentence kept. You never approve by command, button or by reading what the AI wrote; you are asked only to arbitrate when new intent contradicts older intent, and you undo a judge's approval by saying so.
will: Keep each sentence of yours with the context it was said in as a pre-intent, and link every formal record back to it.
Approve a record on your behalf once the judge cascade validates the agent's interpretation, marked judge-approved everywhere.
Put a contradiction between new and older intent, a merge conflict included, to you as one question through the question tool or the browser study room, the agent's recommendation first.
Count only words plumb itself saw from you; another session, a notification, hook text or the agent's relay never counts.
Send any edit to an approved record, a changed acceptance test included, back through the judge.
wont: An approval command, a confirm command, or any owner command that takes a record id.
Read-back cards or buttons you read and press to approve what the AI wrote.
The agent deciding on its own reading that you approved, or relaying your answer into a record.
Fixed word lists deciding what your answer means.
assumptions: The judge cascade itself (JEV above 0.9, else Sonnet asks, then JEV again) is defined under P9; P3 only says its verdict counts as approval.
Answers given through the question tool or the browser study room are read by plumb from the host's own record, not from the agent's restatement.
Internal CLI steps may still name ids for the agent; only approval-writing steps are refused to it.
A merge conflict stays the owner's to arbitrate even when the agent is confident (P11); confidence only orders the options.

requirements.title: An approval pins the exact content approved; any later edit goes back to the judge
requirements.statement: An approval, the owner's or the judge's, pins the hash of the record and of each acceptance test verifying it. While the pin matches the record is approved; never approved or reversed by the owner, it is proposed. Any later edit, a changed acceptance test included, makes it an unconfirmed edit that goes back through the judge cascade, held at the merge until approved again.

examples.given: an approved requirement
examples.then: it shows as an unconfirmed edit, not approved, and is handed back to the judge cascade

examples.given: a requirement never approved
examples.then: it is proposed

examples.then: it returns to proposed, citing the owner's words

proof.plan: Recommended: in a scratch repository the owner sees a judge-approved requirement; the agent edits its statement and the status shows it as an unconfirmed edit until the judge approves it again; then the owner says in conversation that it is wrong and it returns to proposed. The owner decides whether this run is the proof.

requirements.title: A hidden regression of an approved example holds until the test that passed before passes again
requirements.statement: When an approved example's acceptance test is changed so that a regression now passes, plumb names it a hidden regression: the stop hook blocks the agent once naming the example, the turn-end line, status and drift name it, and the merge check lists the changed test and the regression and exits 5. It resolves only when the test body that passed before passes again. Wanting the example's outcome to change is a change of older intent, put to the owner through the question tool. An acceptance test extended with no regression only goes back through the judge cascade.

examples.given: an approved requirement whose example "given a=1 and b=2 ... then it returns 3" is verified by tests/test_mod.py, a passing full run, then add() changed to subtract and the run reporting the regression
examples.when: the agent rewrites the test to assert add(1, 2) == -1, it passes, and the merge check runs
examples.then: it lists the requirement as "(acceptance test changed)" with the example and the test diff, lists the failing acceptance test as "regression, hidden", and exits 5

examples.then: both name the changed acceptance test and the hidden regression

examples.given: an approved acceptance test extended with a new passing test, no regression
examples.then: the requirement waits as "acceptance test changed", goes back through the judge cascade, and the merge exits 4 until the judge approves it; the owner is not asked

examples.given: a regression on test body h1
examples.when: a pass comes on test body h2, then a pass on h1
examples.then: the first pass marks it hidden; only the pass on h1 resolves it

examples.when: the agent wants the example's outcome to change
examples.then: plumb treats it as a change of older intent and asks the owner through the question tool; the merge holds until the original test passes again or the owner agrees

proof.plan: Recommended: in a scratch repository the owner sees a judge-approved requirement, the agent rewrites its acceptance test to hide a regression, and the merge check names the changed test and the hidden regression and holds; then the original test passes again and the hold lifts. The owner decides whether this run, or its recorded transcript, is the proof.

requirements.title: Only words plumb itself saw from the owner count, kept as a pre-intent with their context
requirements.statement: The prompt log records each entry's origin as the host marks it. Only the owner's typed message, or their answer read from the host's record of a question-tool call or from the study room, counts as the owner's words, kept with its context as a pre-intent. Another session's message, a task notification, hook text, the agent's relay or conclusion never counts: it moves no gate and backs no pre-intent, answer or approval. An approval resting on a message the agent logged itself, on a host with no prompt hook, is labelled self-recorded wherever it is shown; plumb's installed skills tell the agent it never decides on its own that the owner approved, and name no relay.

requirements.title: A judge-validated interpretation approves on the owner's behalf; there is no approval command
requirements.statement: The agent rewords the owner's pre-intent into formal records; the judge cascade validates that interpretation against the owner's words and context, and a validated record is approved on the owner's behalf, marked judge-approved, with the trail from pre-intent to record. The owner approves nothing by command, button or read-back card and is asked only to arbitrate contradictory intent. No word list decides anything.

requirements.title: The agent can never write an approval
requirements.statement: Only the judge worker's entries and plumb's reading of the owner's own answers write an approval. Every approval-writing step the agent runs (approve, confirm, revoke, relay, posting a study-room answer) is refused with exit 3 and writes nothing, also on a host that cannot mark the agent's session; an approval entry written by hand is rejected by validation.

requirements.title: The owner arbitrates a conflict through a question, with the agent's recommendation first
requirements.statement: A conflict between two versions of intent is put to the owner as one question through the question tool, or in the browser study room when there is more to study. The agent may store a suggested resolution (one side, or a combined version) with a one-line reason; it is shown first, marked recommended, and chooses nothing. plumb reads the owner's answer, or a chat reply that clearly picks a version, by meaning; the agent never relays it.

decisions.question: Which edit to an approved record loses its approval?
decisions.chosen: Every edit, a changed acceptance test included; it goes back through the judge cascade, and the owner is asked only when the edit changes older intent.
alternatives: Only an edit that changes an example's then-clause; a rewording keeps the record approved.
The owner reconfirms every edit, asked once per principle.

decisions.question: What counts as the owner's words and answers?
decisions.chosen: Only what plumb saw itself: the owner's own typed message read by meaning, an answer read from the host's record of a question-tool call, or an answer given in the browser study room; a judge-validated interpretation of those words approves on the owner's behalf. The agent never carries an answer.
alternatives: Also words the agent relays, checked by a model.
Anything the agent reports the owner agreed to.
Card presses and typed approval commands naming ids.

decisions.question: How is approval writing kept from the agent?
decisions.chosen: The session marker refuses every approval-writing and answer-posting step in the agent's shell, an agent shell without a terminal is refused too, a study-room answer carries a secret only the study room holds, and a hand-written approval entry is never accepted; only the judge worker and plumb's reading of the owner's answers write approvals.
alternatives: A PreToolUse hook on every shell call.

decisions.question: Where are the owner's logged words kept?
decisions.chosen: The prompt hook writes {digest, session, at, origin, text} to gitignored session state; when a pre-intent or an approval cites them, their digest and the sentence with its context are copied into the committed record trail.
alternatives: The prompt hook writes every prompt to a committed log.

decisions.question: Where does the owner answer a merge conflict?
decisions.chosen: Through the question tool, or the browser study room when there is more to study, or in chat read by plumb by meaning; the choice applies only when the answer clearly picks one version.

retired_decisions.why: plumb relay no longer exists and there is no approval command (P3): no command records an approval the agent relays
